strategy: Add one project-local durable external-event scheduler below the Concrete Host factory. It will ingest only events matching the exact active WAITING_EXTERNAL session, bind them to the Host revision and TaskRun wait checkpoint, persist immutable event evidence, serialize delivery per session, and call the existing Starter Host transport for RESUME_EXTERNAL or RECONCILE. A one-shot CLI supports ingest, wake, and bounded run-once; it never polls providers or becomes a daemon. Upgrade the closed bootstrap and initializer to generate its roots and fixed non-authorizing policy.

unchanged_boundaries: EventDrivenCIProviderAdapter remains Provider-specific event interpretation authority
StarterHostOrchestrator remains Host session ordering and resume correlation authority
StarterHostCommandTransport remains the closed RESUME_EXTERNAL and RECONCILE wire owner
LangGraph remains Workflow sequence and declared route owner
WorkflowTaskRunBridge and TaskRun remain lifecycle and completion authorities
ChangePermit Write Authority and Human Gate adapters remain unchanged
provider listeners authenticate and normalize their own external source before generic ingest
customer application source and production dependencies remain independent
forbidden_repairs: Do not add provider polling, sleep loops, background threads, or a second Workflow runtime.
Do not mutate Host session or TaskRun files directly from the scheduler.
Do not accept an event that fails exact provider, correlation, event-name, session revision, TaskRun, or wait-checkpoint binding.
Do not deliver two events concurrently to one Host session or blindly retry an uncertain transition.
Do not let scheduler configuration, event arrival, CI green, or delivery receipts grant write, Quality, completion, release, production, or merge authority.
Do not add GitHub-specific semantics to the generic scheduler.
Do not change services, web, contracts, or standalone application dependencies.
required_invariants: ingest is legal only against one exact persisted WAITING_EXTERNAL Host session and TaskRun checkpoint
event identity is deterministic and its immutable bytes are fingerprinted
one per-session lock serializes competing event deliveries
delivery invokes only existing RESUME_EXTERNAL or exact pending-transition RECONCILE
duplicate wake returns one durable delivery receipt without a second resume
a crash after TaskRun resume can be proven from exact event evidence; ambiguous state fails closed
run-once is bounded and contains no provider polling loop
Graph END remains TaskRun VALIDATING and scheduler policy remains non-authorizing

focused: exact waiting event ingests and wakes the same session/TaskRun through existing transport
duplicate and concurrent wake produce one resume and one durable receipt
counterexamples: wrong provider, correlation, event name, evidence, session, revision, TaskRun, or wait checkpoint is rejected
a second event for an already-consumed wait is rejected stale
tampered event, reservation, receipt, or path fails closed
regression: provider adapter, LangGraph runtime, TaskRun bridge, Host orchestrator/transport, initializer, schema, and all skill-only profiles remain green
negative_path: scheduler contains no polling loop and cannot complete TaskRun or merge
product source and dependencies remain unchanged

risks: Generic ingest assumes the caller is a trusted provider listener that already authenticated the webhook or provider API response; provider signature verification remains provider-specific.
An event arriving before the Host publishes its exact wait is intentionally rejected and must be retried by the listener after the wait exists.
Local filesystem durability is suitable for one project Host instance; multi-node deployment will require a future database-backed scheduler adapter with the same contract.
rollback_plan: Remove the scheduler module, CLI route, @3 scheduler fields, schemas, tests, and docs; restore concrete-host-bootstrap@2 while leaving the existing manual RESUME_EXTERNAL, LangGraph checkpoint, TaskRun bridge, Provider adapter, Write Authority, and Human Gate behavior unchanged.
